headline: Peter Thiel’s fund held eight stocks. Seven were energy companies.
dek: Thiel Macro’s Q2 2026 13F reported $418.67M across eight U.S.-listed stocks. Amazon was the largest position. The other seven were oil, power, utility and nuclear-technology companies.
cardSummary: Amazon plus seven energy companies: oil, power generation, regulated utilities and nuclear technology.

sections.heading: A tech investor, an energy-heavy filing
paragraphs: Peter Thiel co-founded PayPal and Palantir and was Facebook’s first outside investor. Thiel Macro’s Q2 2026 13F looked different. It reported $418.67M across eight stocks, and seven of them were energy companies: oil production, power generation, regulated utilities and nuclear technology.
This is the U.S.-listed portfolio that Thiel Macro LLC disclosed. It is not Founders Fund’s portfolio and not Peter Thiel’s total investments.

sections.heading: Amazon on the demand side
paragraphs: [Amazon](company:amazon) was the largest position at 28.18% of the reported 13F value, or $117.98M. Its AWS business supplies computing, storage and AI infrastructure. That puts Amazon on the demand side of the data-center buildout, next to seven companies that produce or deliver energy.

sections.heading: Seven different energy businesses
paragraphs: [Vista Energy](company:vista-energy) (VIST), an oil and gas producer focused on Argentina’s Vaca Muerta shale, was second at 18.13%. [Vistra](company:vistra) (VST), a U.S. power producer with nuclear and natural-gas plants, was third at 14.12%. The names and tickers are close, but they are different companies.

Four regulated utilities came next: [American Electric Power](company:american-electric-power), [DTE Energy](company:dte-energy), [FirstEnergy](company:firstenergy) and [CMS Energy](company:cms-energy). Each was between 9.45% and 10.08%, and together they were 38.69%.

[X-energy](company:x-energy), which develops small modular nuclear reactors, was the smallest position at 0.88%. Its SEC industry code is fabricated plate work (SIC 3443), not utilities. We count it as energy because its business is reactor development.

sections.heading: Energy was 71.82% of the filing
paragraphs: Together the seven energy holdings were 71.82% of the reported value. This was not one uniform bet on AI electricity demand. The holdings have different exposure to regulation, power prices and oil prices.
The energy emphasis is our reading of the disclosed holdings. Thiel Macro has not stated a reason for any of these positions.

sections.heading: All eight are new since Q1
paragraphs: Thiel Macro’s Q1 2026 report listed no positions, so all eight holdings are new compared with Q1. Vistra is a return: the Q2 2025 report listed 208,747 Vistra shares.

cover.headline: Thiel’s fund goes heavy on energy
cover.body: Peter Thiel’s fund held eight stocks. Seven were energy companies.

intro.title: A tech investor. An energy-heavy filing.
intro.body: Peter Thiel co-founded PayPal and Palantir and was Facebook’s first outside investor. But Thiel Macro’s Q2 filing was dominated by energy: oil production, power generation, regulated utilities and nuclear technology.

outro.title: Energy was 71.82% of the filing.
outro.body: Four regulated utilities alone accounted for 38.69%. Vistra added power generation, Vista Energy Argentine oil, X-energy nuclear technology.

holdingNotes.x-energy: X-energy develops small modular nuclear reactors and specialized nuclear fuel. Its Xe-100 program targets reliable electricity and industrial heat, adding exposure to developing nuclear technology rather than an established utility network.
holdingNotes.cms-energy: CMS Energy owns Consumers Energy, a Michigan electricity and natural-gas utility. Its generation assets, power grid and gas network add another regulated utility to a portfolio already heavily exposed to energy.
holdingNotes.firstenergy: FirstEnergy operates electric utilities and transmission infrastructure across the Midwest and Mid-Atlantic. Its business centers on delivering power and maintaining the grid, giving the portfolio another regulated-infrastructure holding.
holdingNotes.dte-energy: DTE supplies electricity and natural gas in Michigan through its regulated utilities. Its generation, grid and gas-network investments make this a holding in everyday energy delivery, not a speculative reactor developer.
holdingNotes.american-electric-power: AEP generates, transmits and distributes electricity across an extensive U.S. utility network. Its power lines and regulated utility investments connect rising electricity demand with the infrastructure needed to deliver it.
holdingNotes.vistra: Vistra generates and sells electricity through nuclear, natural-gas and other power assets, alongside retail electricity brands. It adds competitive power-generation exposure rather than the regulated grid businesses held elsewhere in this portfolio.
holdingNotes.vista-energy: Vista produces oil and natural gas, with a major focus on Argentina’s Vaca Muerta shale formation. Unlike the electric utilities in this portfolio, its business is tied directly to hydrocarbon production and commodity prices.
holdingNotes.amazon: Amazon combines online retail with AWS, its cloud-computing business. AWS supplies computing, storage and AI infrastructure, placing Amazon on the demand side of the data-center buildout alongside the portfolio’s energy suppliers.
